scope: Targeted curated primary-source research; not a systematic review of thousands of papers.

sources.title: Air Quality Gas Sensor (Model: MQ135) Manual, version 1.6
authors: Zhengzhou Winsen Electronics Technology Co., Ltd.
sources.claim_supported: SnO2 response is broad and temperature/humidity dependent; Rs=(Vc/VRL-1)RL. Requires regulated 5 V heater, up to 950 mW, and over 48 h initial preheat.
sources.read_depth: Manufacturer PDF: specifications, circuit, response and cautions read.
sources.limitations: Does not establish selective CO2 measurement or rover accuracy. No manual figures reused; copyrighted.

sources.title: Carbon Monoxide Gas Sensor (Model: MQ-7B) Manual, version 1.6
authors: Zhengzhou Winsen Electronics Technology Co., Ltd.
sources.claim_supported: MQ-7B uses 60 s at 5 V heating followed by 90 s at 1.5 V; CO sensing occurs in low-temperature phase. Initial preheat is at least 48 h.
sources.read_depth: Manufacturer PDF: operating sequence, specifications, circuit and cautions read.
sources.limitations: The rover description says MQ7, not MQ-7B. Verify exact sensor and module before transferring these timing/voltage/range specifications.

sources.title: Flammable Gas Sensor (Model: MQ-4) Manual, version 1.6
authors: Zhengzhou Winsen Electronics Technology Co., Ltd.
sources.claim_supported: MQ-4 is a heated SnO2 methane-sensitive sensor; manufacturer lists CH4 range 300–10000 ppm and a regulated 5 V heater.
sources.read_depth: Manufacturer PDF introductory/specification sections and official product listing read.
sources.limitations: Range is not an accuracy statement; ppm estimation needs unit-specific calibration and interference evaluation.

sources.title: BMP180 Digital Pressure Sensor Data Sheet, revision 2.5, BST-BMP180-DS000-09
sources.claim_supported: Pressure/temperature outputs require sensor-specific EEPROM compensation; housing must be vented and protected from liquids/light/rapid heat changes. It does not measure humidity.
sources.read_depth: Manufacturer PDF sections 3.1–3.6 and 6.5 read. Distributor-hosted original manufacturer document.
sources.limitations: Do not infer air humidity from BMP180. Barometric altitude depends on reference pressure and weather.

sources.title: GUVA-S12SD UV Detection Sensor (TOY0044)
sources.claim_supported: GUVA-S12SD reference module detects 200–370 nm; module output conversion depends on analogue gain and calibration.
sources.read_depth: Official product specification page read.
sources.limitations: TOY0044 is one GUVA-S12SD module, not a verified identification of the rover board. Spectral/angle calibration is needed before reporting defensible UV index.

sources.title: Gravity: Analog pH Sensor V2 (SEN0161-V2)
sources.claim_supported: Official reference implementation recommends two-point buffer calibration to identify both offset and slope; fresh standards and repeated calibration are required.
sources.read_depth: Official specifications and calibration FAQ read.
sources.limitations: Reference design only: supplied rover description does not identify the actual pH module model.

sources.title: Gravity: Analog Turbidity Sensor (SEN0189)
sources.claim_supported: Reference optical turbidity module provides analogue voltage or threshold output; voltage must be independently calibrated for quantitative interpretation.
sources.read_depth: Official specifications, reference description and pinout read.
sources.limitations: Reference design only; rover turbidity sensor model unverified. Do not equate generic voltage conversion with validated NTU or drinking-water safety.

sources.title: The influence of humidity on the performance of a low-cost air particle mass sensor and the effect of atmospheric fog
sources.claim_supported: Humidity and fog increase apparent optical PM readings; PMS1003 laboratory deviations began around 75–80% RH.
sources.read_depth: Full publisher HTML: methods, laboratory results, field results, Figure 2 and license.
sources.limitations: PMS1003 evidence is mechanistically relevant but not a PMS7003 calibration.

sources.title: Field evaluation of low-cost particulate matter sensors in high- and low-concentration environments
sources.claim_supported: PMS3003 performance was evaluated across low/high concentration and seasonal environments; calibration and averaging affect usefulness.
sources.read_depth: Publisher abstract and methods excerpts; Crossref metadata.
sources.limitations: Different Plantower model and field sites; performance is not transferable to A3P5.

sources.title: Gaussian process regression model for dynamically calibrating and surveilling a wireless low-cost particulate matter sensor network in Delhi
sources.claim_supported: A PMS7003-based Delhi network used Gaussian-process and linear calibration with reference stations; sensor siting preserves free airflow and environmental covariates.
sources.read_depth: Publisher HTML: hardware, calibration equations, validation and Figure 4; metadata and license.
sources.limitations: Network-scale 2018 study, not evidence of rover mapping precision or a ready-to-use local calibration.

sources.title: Towards a hygroscopic growth calibration for low-cost PM 2.5 sensors
sources.claim_supported: Seasonally varying humidity correction addresses hygroscopic-growth bias in PMS5003 measurements; residual uncertainty remains.
sources.read_depth: Publisher HTML: Eq.1, methods, evaluation, Figures 3–4 and license.
sources.limitations: Sensor model, aerosol mixture and geography differ. Fit local correction coefficients rather than copying study coefficients.

sources.title: Development and application of a United States-wide correction for PM 2.5 data collected with the PurpleAir sensor
sources.claim_supported: A relative-humidity term improved PurpleAir calibration; evaluation held out dates and states, and transferability remained geographically limited.
sources.read_depth: Publisher abstract, model-development/validation/limitations sections, Figure 4 and license.
sources.limitations: US PMS5003/PurpleAir correction is not automatically applicable to a single PMS7003 on a moving rover.

sources.title: GADEN: A 3D Gas Dispersion Simulator for Mobile Robot Olfaction in Realistic Environments
sources.claim_supported: GADEN combines 3D wind/filament dispersion and simulated gas sensors to test robotic olfaction in realistic geometry.
sources.read_depth: Original author project documentation, citation metadata; article abstract level.
sources.limitations: Blender staging is not GADEN/CFD simulation and cannot supply validated concentration fields.

sources.title: Information-Driven Gas Distribution Mapping for Autonomous Mobile Robots
sources.claim_supported: Information-driven mapping combines gas/wind probabilistic maps with action selection by expected information; wind-tunnel and simulation evaluation support the method.
sources.read_depth: Primary paper indexed full-text sections 1,3,4,5 and conclusions; Crossref metadata.
sources.limitations: Requires localization, wind data and computation not established on current A3P5 electronics; proposed future architecture.

sources.title: Scalable Gas Sensing, Mapping, and Path Planning via Decentralized Hilbert Maps
sources.claim_supported: Decentralized Hilbert maps provide scalable gas mapping and information-driven path planning for distributed sensors.
sources.read_depth: Publisher/PubMed abstracts and Crossref metadata.
sources.limitations: Background method only; no decentralized map implemented or validated here.

sources.title: Towards the Development of an Affordable and Practical Light Attenuation Turbidity Sensor for Remote Near Real-Time Aquatic Monitoring
sources.claim_supported: Independent turbidity calibration, waterproofing and fouling management are essential; the study re-engineered Gravity-type sensing and validated against Formazin/turbidimeter standards.
sources.read_depth: Publisher full HTML: sections 3–5, experimental figures and license.
sources.limitations: Study-specific electronics and usable range differ. Generic vendor calibration is not rover validation.

sources.title: A Compact, Low-Cost, and Low-Power Turbidity Sensor for Continuous In Situ Stormwater Monitoring
sources.claim_supported: A low-cost stormwater turbidity system was tested in laboratory/field; pre-/post-cleaning calibration exposed fouling and drift effects.
sources.read_depth: Publisher indexed full methods/results/limitations excerpts and Crossref metadata.
sources.limitations: Different sensor geometry. Its quoted cost, range and accuracy must not be assigned to A3P5.

sources.title: Development of a Robotic Airboat for Online Water Quality Monitoring in Lakes
sources.claim_supported: An autonomous surface vehicle provides a precedent for geolocated online water-quality sampling.
sources.read_depth: Publisher abstract and Crossref metadata.
sources.limitations: Aquatic airboat, not ground rover. Do not imply A3P5 is amphibious.

sources.title: Leakage and the reproducibility crisis in machine-learning-based science
sources.claim_supported: Training/test leakage can produce optimistic scientific ML results; explicit model-information reporting exposes leakage pathways.
sources.read_depth: Primary article abstract, framework and resource-availability excerpts; author repository; Crossref metadata.
sources.limitations: Supports validation design rather than any model score.

sources.title: Cross‐validation strategies for data with temporal, spatial, hierarchical, or phylogenetic structure
sources.claim_supported: Validation should respect temporal, spatial and group dependencies; blocking must match the intended prediction task.
sources.read_depth: Primary author paper abstract and methodological recommendations; publisher metadata.
sources.limitations: Methodological synthesis, classified as a review by the publisher; not an A3P5 experiment.

sources.title: Random Forests
sources.claim_supported: Random forests aggregate randomized decision trees; suitable as a proposed nonlinear baseline after data collection.
sources.read_depth: Original publisher abstract and Crossref metadata.
sources.limitations: No random forest has been trained on rover logs.

sources.title: Isolation-Based Anomaly Detection
sources.claim_supported: Isolation Forest detects unusual observations through their ease of isolation in random trees.
sources.read_depth: Original publisher abstract, author manuscript overview and Crossref metadata.
sources.limitations: An anomaly score identifies unusualness, not a confirmed pollutant or environmental hazard.
sources.journal: ACM Transactions on Knowledge Discovery from Data

sources.title: Gaussian Processes for Machine Learning
sources.claim_supported: Gaussian-process regression represents a latent function with a covariance kernel and yields conditional predictions and uncertainty.
sources.read_depth: Authors official book contents and regression chapter synopsis; publisher metadata.
sources.limitations: Book cited as 2006 per title-page convention; online publisher release metadata is November 2005. No fitted rover GP exists.

sources.title: Laboratory and field evaluation of a low-cost methane sensor and key environmental factors for sensor calibration
sources.claim_supported: Unit-specific calibration and CO, temperature and humidity covariates affected low-cost methane performance; seasonal validation changed results.
sources.read_depth: Primary publisher abstract and license read.
sources.limitations: Study sensor was Figaro TGS2600, not MQ4. Evidence supports calibration/interference testing, not transferred accuracy.

sources.title: Chapter A6.4. Measurement of pH
sources.claim_supported: Field pH measurement requires instrument calibration, maintenance, stabilization, quality assurance and documented reporting.
sources.read_depth: Official report abstract, scope and table of contents; measurement-method summary.
sources.limitations: Use its procedures as the validation basis; a pH reading alone does not establish potability.
